name: Ebed-melech
overview: Ebed-melech was a male Ethiopian eunuch known for his courageous intervention on behalf of the prophet Jeremiah. His distinct identity as a foreign court official highlights his unique role in the biblical narrative. Scripture identifies him specifically as the Ethiopian eunuch who spoke up for Jeremiah, underscoring his faithfulness and boldness.
namesAndTitles: The name Ebed-melech means 'servant of Melek [king] or Malk' in Hebrew, indicating his position as a servant or official under royal authority. This proper name is not recorded as being given directly by God but reflects his role within the king's court.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Ebed-melech beyond what is indicated by his unique attribute as an Ethiopian eunuch who supported Jeremiah. No additional familial connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ebed-melech's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his faithful advocacy for the prophet Jeremiah during a time of great danger. His willingness to speak up on Jeremiah's behalf demonstrates a Christ-like courage and compassion, serving as an example of godly boldness and loyalty within a foreign context. His actions contribute to the preservation of God's messenger and the ongoing fulfillment of divine purposes.
